heading: Asian Games 2026 Day 2 Medal Tally: Where India stands after four more medals as China continue to dominate in Aichi-Nagoya
author: Edited by: Hijam Raju Singh / TIMESOFINDIA.COM /  Sep 21, 2026, 19:16 IST
paragraphs: NEW DELHI: India's wait for a gold medal continued on Day 2 of the Asian Games 2026, but four more podium finishes lifted the country's tally to six as shooting once again led the charge in Aichi-Nagoya

India added three medals from the range and a historic bronze in mixed martial arts to move to four silver and two bronze medals overall.India were placed 12th in the medal standings at the end of the day's action, while China continued to set the pace at the top of the table

Japan and South Korea remained in the leading pack as the early medal race began to take shape.Shooting delivers three more medalsThe shooting range once again proved to be India's most productive venue

Himanshu Dhillon and Rudrankksh Patil secured silver and bronze respectively in the men's 10m air rifle individual event, while the duo combined with Parth Mane to win the team silver.Dhillon held his nerve to finish second behind China's Olympic champion Sheng Lihao, who successfully defended his Asian Games title with 254.2 points

The results took India's shooting tally to five medals — four silver and one bronze — after the two silver medals won by Elavenil Valarivan and her teammates on the opening day.ALSO READ: India win four medals as shooting delivers three and Suchika Tariyal makes MMA history amid heartbreakSuchika makes MMA history amid heartbreakThe fourth Indian medal of the day came from Suchika Tariyal, who created history by becoming India's first Asian Games medallist in mixed martial arts
But the bronze came with a painful twist.Suchika's semifinal against Singapore's Hui Hoon Teo ended in a draw, but the Indian was around 700 grams heavier at the morning weigh-in

Under the competition rules, the lighter athlete advances when a bout is tied, sending Teo into the final and leaving Suchika with the bronze.China strengthen grip on medal tableChina's dominance was reflected across several venues

In swimming, 13-year-old Yu Zidi won her second gold medal in as many days, setting an Asian Games record in the women's 200m individual medley.China also won gold in the men's 100m breaststroke through Dong Zhihao, while Qin Haiyang took bronze

The results added to China's growing haul - 38 medals including 23 gold, as the continental powerhouse continued to establish a substantial lead over Japan (32 medals) and South Korea (23 medals).For India, the six-medal tally provides a solid start, but the absence of a gold remains the most notable feature of the early standings
